extracted.intended_audience: advanced high-school and early undergraduate students interested in number theory and elliptic curves (e.g., math-olymiad / IMO-level students)
extracted.subtask_short: teaching elliptic curves to advanced students
extracted.subtask_description: A pedagogical chapter explaining preliminaries (abstract algebra, linear algebra, complex analysis) and introducing elliptic curves, their group law, torsion points, Tate modules, and related constructions aimed at making FLT-related ideas accessible to advanced high-school and early-undergraduate readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group (Definition 6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A group is a set G with a binary operation * that is associative, has an identity element e (a * e = a = e * a for all a in G), and every element has an inverse (for each a there exists b with a * b = e = b * a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis: invertibility is the key property. Examples: invertible functions under composition. Consequences such as uniqueness of identity and inverses follow (Lemma 6.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgroup (Definition 6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A subgroup H of a group G is a subset closed under the group operation and which itself forms a group under the restricted operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closure under the operation suffices along with inheriting identity and inverses from G; used to identify natural substructures (e.g., torsion subgroups).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abelian Group (Definition 6.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Abelian group is a group whose operation is commutative: a * b = b * a for all a, b in G. Usually written additively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common examples: (Z, +), Z/nZ. Many constructions (e.g., group law on elliptic curves) yield Abelian groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclic Group (Definition 6.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A (finite) cyclic group is generated by a single element: every element can be obtained by repeatedly applying the operation to one generator (e.g., Z/nZ generated by 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes finite vs infinite cyclic groups (Z is infinite cyclic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalar Multiplication by Integers (Definition 6.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an Abelian group G and n in Z, define n·g = g + g + ... + g (n times) for n ≥ 0, and (−n)·g = −(n·g) for n < 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets up notion of torsion and module-like structure over Z.

rubrics_metrics.name: Torsion Subgroup (Definition 6.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an Abelian group G, G[n] = { g in G : n g = 0 } is the n-torsion subgroup; the torsion subgroup G_tors = union over n of G[n] consists of elements of finite order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key milestone: torsion points of an elliptic curve; examples and role in later module/Tate constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct Sum of Abelian Groups (Definition 6.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given Abelian groups A and B, A ⊕ B consists of ordered pairs (a,b) with pointwise addition (a1,b1)+(a2,b2)=(a1+a2,b1+b2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to express decompositions like E[n] ≅ Z/nZ ⊕ Z/nZ and to build larger groups from smaller ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ring (Definition 6.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: A ring R has two operations + and × with (R,+) an Abelian group, multiplication associative, and distributivity holds: a×(b+c)=a×b + a×c etc. Often includes a multiplicative identity; commutative rings have commutative multiplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rings have addition, subtraction and multiplication but not necessarily division; examples include Z and Z/nZ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field (Definition 6.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: A field F is a commutative ring in which every non-zero element has a multiplicative inverse; equivalently (F,+) is an Abelian group and (F\{0},×) is an Abelian group with distributivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Q, C, F_p = Z/pZ when p is prime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic of a Field (Definition 6.10 & Proposition 6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The characteristic of a field is the smallest positive integer n such that n·1 = 0 (scaling 1 by n); if no such n exists the characteristic is 0. If non-zero, the characteristic must be prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important constraints: many transformations (e.g., dividing by 2 or 3) require char(F) ≠ 2 or 3. Examples: Q and C have characteristic 0, F_p has characteristic p.

rubrics_metrics.name: R-module (Definition 6.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R be a ring with 1. An (left) R-module V is an Abelian group (V,+) equipped with scalar multiplication R × V → V satisfying distributivity and compatibility: λ·(v1+v2)=λ·v1+λ·v2, (r1+r2)·v=r1·v+r2·v, (r1r2)·v=r1·(r2·v), 1·v=v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vector spaces are modules over fields; examples: every Abelian group is a Z-module. This viewpoint is used for torsion points as Z/p-modules = F_p-vector spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: F-vector space (Definition 6.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: A vector space over a field F is an F-module (module where R=F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to view E[p] as an F_p-vector space and to discuss dimensions (e.g., two-dimensional).

rubrics_metrics.name: Module Direct Sum and Scaling (Definition 6.1/Example 6.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given R-modules U and V, define U ⊕ V with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication λ(u,v)=(λu,λv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when showing decompositions of torsion/submodule structures such as F_p ⊕ F_p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group Homomorphism (Definition 6.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: A function φ : G → H between groups is a homomorphism if φ(ab)=φ(a)φ(b) for all a,b in G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: homomorphisms preserve identity and inverses; used to define maps φ_n : E[ℓ^{n+1}] → E[ℓ^n] by multiplication-by-ℓ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group Isomorphism and Automorphism (Definitions 6.14–6.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: An isomorphism is a bijective homomorphism (G ≅ H). An automorphism is an isomorphism of a group to itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isomorphism captures 'same structure up to renaming'; examples: Aut(F) for field automorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ring Homomorphism (Section 6.2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A ring homomorphism φ : R → S preserves addition and multiplication: φ(a+b)=φ(a)+φ(b), φ(ab)=φ(a)φ(b); often one also requires φ(1_R)=1_S but not always.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: canonical map Z → Z/nZ is a ring homomorphism; field automorphisms (e.g., complex conjugation) are ring/field homomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Module Homomorphism (Section 6.2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: An R-module homomorphism f : M → N preserves addition and scalar multiplication: f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y), f(r x)=r f(x) for all x,y in M and r in R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in relating module structures on torsion points and Tate modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weierstrass Equation (Definition 7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a field F and constants a1,a2,a3,a4,a6 in F, the (general) Weierstrass equation is y^2 + a1 x y + a3 y = x^3 + a2 x^2 + a4 x + a6, whose solutions define an elliptic curve (with added point at infinity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the starting algebraic equation; transformations can simplify it to short Weierstrass forms under characteristic restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short Weierstrass / change-of-variables (Proposition 7.1 & Theorems 7.1–7.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: By linear changes of variables (requiring division by 2 and/or 3), one can transform the general Weierstrass equation to forms y^2 = x^3 + A x + B when char(F) ≠ 2,3 (intermediate form y^2 = 4x^3 − c4 x − c6 also shown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must avoid fields of characteristic 2 or 3 when dividing by 2 or 3; explicit formulas for coefficients (b2,b4,b6,c4,c6, A,B) are provided in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminant of short Weierstrass (Lemma 7.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For y^2 = x^3 + A x + B, the discriminant is ∆ = −16(4A^3 + 27B^2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-vanishing of ∆ is tied to non-singularity; minimal Weierstrass equation over Q chosen to minimize the p-adic valuation of ∆ when reducing mod p.

rubrics_metrics.name: j-invariant (Definition 7.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The j-invariant is j = 1728 c4^3 / ∆ where c4 is the coefficient from the transformed equation and ∆ the discriminant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two elliptic curves are isomorphic over an algebraically closed field iff they have the same j-invariant (used as an invariant distinguishing curves).

rubrics_metrics.name: Elliptic Curve Group Law (Theorem 7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define addition on an elliptic curve E with point at infinity O by: P + Q = R iff P, Q, −R are collinear, with conventions: line through O and P is vertical; if P=Q≠O the line is tangent at P. This operation makes E an Abelian group with identity O and negative of R given by reflecting y-coordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketch: intersection with line gives a cubic whose third root provides rationality of coordinates; group axioms verified (commutativity, identity O, inverses via reflection, associativity delegated to appendix).

rubrics_metrics.name: Group axioms satisfaction for elliptic curve addition
rubrics_metrics.description: Properties to verify: commutativity (line through P,Q same as Q,P), identity (O is identity via vertical line argument), inverses (−P = (x,−y) lies on curve), associativity (lengthy proof, not included here).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associativity is non-trivial and deferred to an appendix; rationality arguments use Vieta's formulae and rational coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formula for x-coordinate of addition (Proposition 7.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If P=(xP,yP), Q=(xQ,yQ) and P+Q=R on y^2 = x^3 + A x + B, then x_R = ( (y_Q − y_P)/(x_Q − x_P) )^2 − x_P − x_Q (suitably adapted for slope/m tangent cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derivation via intersection of the line y = m x + b with the cubic and Vieta relations; slope m = (yQ − yP)/(xQ − xP).

rubrics_metrics.name: m-torsion points E[m] and p-division points (Proposition 7.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: E[m] = { P in E : m P = O } is the m-torsion subgroup; for prime p, E[p] with scalar multiplication mod p is an F_p-vector space (the p-division points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These torsion subgroups are central to Galois/Tate module constructions and behave like (Z/nZ) ⊕ (Z/nZ) for n-torsion (see Theorem 7.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplication-by-ℓ homomorphisms and inverse systems (φ_n maps)
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed prime ℓ, define φ_n : E[ℓ^{n+1}] → E[ℓ^n] by φ_n(P) = ℓ P. These maps make the torsion groups into an inverse system used to form inverse limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surjectivity of φ_n (multiplication-by-ℓ) is used later to construct compatible generators across levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: ℓ-adic integers (Definition 7.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Z_ℓ = lim ← ( Z/ℓ^n Z ) is the inverse limit of Z/ℓ^nZ: sequences (a_n) with a_{n} ≡ a_{n+m} (mod ℓ^n) for all m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides coefficient ring for the Tate module, enabling action of ℓ-adic scalars on inverse-limit torsion sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: ℓ-adic Tate Module (Definition 7.4 & Proposition 7.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tate_ℓ(E) = lim ← E[ℓ^n] = { (P_n)_{n≥1} : P_n in E[ℓ^n], φ_n(P_{n+1})=P_n } is defined as the inverse limit of ℓ^n-division points. It is a Z_ℓ-module with scalar multiplication defined componentwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check compatibility: φ_n is a group homomorphism and sequences (a_n) in Z_ℓ satisfy congruence conditions so componentwise scalar multiplication yields a valid element of Tate_ℓ(E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformisation Theorem and Lattices (Section 7.3 & Definition 7.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Over C, elliptic curves can be uniformised: E(C) ≅ C / L where L = Z ω1 ⊕ Z ω2 is a lattice (ω1,ω2 in C linearly independent over R).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lattices are subgroups of C under addition; the quotient C/L is a complex torus whose group structure matches E(C). This viewpoint is used to analyse torsion points and isomorphisms of E(C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of n-torsion: E[n] ≅ (Z/nZ) ⊕ (Z/nZ) (Theorem 7.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an elliptic curve over C (hence over fields sufficiently nice), the n-torsion subgroup E[n] is isomorphic to (Z/nZ) ⊕ (Z/nZ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses uniformisation: elements correspond to fractions a/n ω1 + b/n ω2; injectivity/surjectivity arguments give bijection; corollary: for prime ℓ, E[ℓ] is 2-dimensional over Z/ℓZ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tate module two-dimensionality (Theorem 7.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tate_ℓ(E) ≅ Z_ℓ ⊕ Z_ℓ, i.e., the Tate module is a free rank-2 Z_ℓ-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: pick compatible generators at each level using surjectivity of φ_n to produce two ℓ-adic generators; more general inverse-limit decomposition results (Proposition 7.6) support this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverse Limit (Definition 7.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an inverse system of groups {A_i} with transition maps f_{ij}: A_j → A_i for i ≤ j satisfying compatibility, the inverse limit lim ← A_i consists of sequences (a_i) with a_i = f_{ij}(a_j) for all j ≥ i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General construction underlying Z_ℓ and Tate modules; preserves direct-sum decompositions when connecting maps respect the decomposition (Proposition 7.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2×2 Matrices and Mat2(R) (Definition 8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 2×2 matrix over a commutative ring R is an array [[a,b],[c,d]] with componentwise addition and a specified multiplication; the set of such matrices is Mat_2(R), which is a ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete linear algebra suited to explicit computations; matrix operations and examples shown. Matrix multiplication is generally non-commutative; identity matrix I = [[1,0],[0,1]].

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix invertibility and identity
rubrics_metrics.description: A matrix X in Mat_2(R) is invertible if there exists Y in Mat_2(R) with XY = YX = I (identity matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invertibility connects to determinant (see below) and defines groups like GL_2(R).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace (Definition 8.2 and Theorem 8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trace Tr(X) of a 2×2 matrix [[a,b],[c,d]] is a + d. For all X,Y in Mat_2, Tr(XY)=Tr(YX); in particular Tr(X Y X^{-1}) = Tr(Y) when X is invertible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace is basis-independent in linear algebra interpretations; it equals the sum of eigenvalues and is invariant under conjugation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinant (Definition 8.3 and Theorem 8.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: det([[a,b],[c,d]]) = ad − bc. Determinant multiplies under multiplication: det(XY)=det(X)det(Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinant is product of eigenvalues and controls invertibility (matrix invertible iff det invertible in base ring).

rubrics_metrics.name: General and Special Linear Groups (Definition 8.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: GL_2(R) is the group of invertible 2×2 matrices over R under multiplication. SL_2(R) is the subgroup of matrices with determinant 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These groups will be considered over various rings (Z, C, Z_ℓ, F_p) and are important for representations and Galois actions later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eigenvectors and Eigenvalues (Definition 8.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For linear T:V→V on an F-vector space V, v≠0 and λ in F satisfy T v = λ v; λ is an eigenvalue and v an eigenvector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characteristic polynomial λ^2 − Tr(T) λ + det(T) gives eigenvalues in 2D; trace is sum of eigenvalues and determinant their product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group Action, Orbit, Stabiliser (Definitions 8.6–8.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: A group action is a map G × X → X with (gh)·x = g·(h·x) and e·x = x. Orbit of x is Gx = { g·x : g in G }. Stabiliser G_x = { g in G : g·x = x } is a subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orbits partition X; transitive actions have one orbit. Actions give homomorphisms from G to permutation groups and are a precursor to linear representations (group as invertible functions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient constructions (Definition 8.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an equivalence relation ∼ on X, X/∼ is the set of equivalence classes. Examples: X/G for group actions (orbits), V/W for vector spaces (quotient by subspace).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotients formalise 'setting things to identity' and appear in constructions like C/L (complex plane modulo a lattice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex Analysis keywords and boundedness (Section 8.3.1 & 8.3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tiered keywords introduced for complex analysis (limits, convergence, holomorphic, poles, Cauchy's theorem, etc.). A bounded function f has |f(z)| < B for some B for all z in its domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex analysis is required for modular forms and uniformisation; the text flags which concepts are Tier One/Two/Three to guide reader preparation.
